page: Amazon Web Services m8i.xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C x86_64 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or a GPU, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong single-core capabilities, with the Geekbench single-core score and single-threaded gzip compression performing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by the stress-ng multi-core CPU and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression benchmarks falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, while small-block cached read bandwidth is weak. Database operations also show weaker performance, though Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput maintain average tiers.

Given its dedicated hardware allocation and DDR5 memory architecture, the m8i.xlarge offers a balanced resource profile for general-purpose workloads. It is suitable for single-threaded applications, web serving, and lightweight text processing. However, its lower multi-core efficiency and lack of local storage make it less optimal for heavy database operations or multi-threaded parallel processing tasks.
